question: 濒死体验证明意识能脱离大脑吗？
question_en: Do near-death experiences prove consciousness can leave the brain?
sub: 是灵魂离体的证据，还是垂死大脑的最后一场烟花？
sub_en: Evidence of a soul departing the body, or the dying brain's last fireworks?

casting.reason: 他从最古怪的病例入手：被截掉的手臂仍在疼，电极一碰右侧颞顶联合区，人就浮到天花板下往下看自己。在他看来，这些现象共同指向一个结论——「我在这具身体里」不是一个前提，而是大脑每秒钟重新算出来的结果。所以离体感证明的是身体图式会出错，不是乘客真的出了门；而「大脑只是接收器」这类说法之所以让他警惕，是因为它不管发现什么脑机制都能自圆其说。
casting.reason_en: He starts from the strangest cases: an amputated arm that still aches; a mild current to the right temporoparietal junction and the patient floats under the ceiling looking down at herself. To him these converge on one conclusion — 'I am inside this body' is not a premise but a result the brain recomputes second by second. So an out-of-body feeling shows that the body schema can misfire, not that a passenger has walked out; and what makes him wary of 'the brain is only a receiver' is that it can absorb any neural finding whatsoever without ever being wrong.

casting.reason: 他守住最强的正题：意识不是脑活动的产物，而是任何活动得以显现的前提。他的支点是熟睡——无梦、无对象、无「我」，醒来却能说「我睡得很沉，什么都不知道」，那个知道自己一无所知的在场者，就是他所说的见证意识。但他同时对濒死体验泼冷水：隧道、故人、光，仍属名色，是幻相里更精致的一层，拿它当梵的证据，等于拿梦里的黄金证明醒着有钱。
casting.reason_en: He holds the strongest affirmative line: consciousness is not a product of brain activity but the precondition of any activity appearing at all. His fulcrum is dreamless sleep — no dream, no object, no 'I', yet on waking one can say 'I slept deeply, I knew nothing'; whoever knew that nothing was known is what he calls the witness. Yet he is cold toward near-death reports: tunnel, dead relatives, light all belong to name-and-form, a finer layer of illusion, and using them as proof of Brahman is like citing gold from a dream as evidence of waking wealth.

casting.reason: 他把一场容易滑向表白的争论拉回可测量的地面：意识进入报告时，脑内出现相当稳定的签名——大范围皮层点燃、约三百毫秒的 P3b、前额与顶叶的长程同步；心脏停跳后，这套签名在几十秒内瓦解。他追问每一方同一句话：什么结果会让你承认自己错了。他也不把实验的空白当作胜利宣言，而更在意它对急救与「宣告死亡」时刻的现实后果。
casting.reason_en: He drags a debate prone to sliding into testimony back onto measurable ground: when a percept enters awareness, the brain shows a fairly stable signature — widespread cortical ignition, a P3b around three hundred milliseconds, long-range frontoparietal synchrony — and after cardiac arrest that signature dissolves within tens of seconds. He puts the same question to every side: what result would make you admit you were wrong. He also refuses to treat an empty experimental record as a victory speech, caring more about what it implies for resuscitation and for the moment death is declared.

casting.reason: 他不站队，而是拆掉双方共用的地基：无论说「脑生识」还是说「识离脑」，都得先承认有一个自性成立的「识」，或可出入、或可断灭。他指出这正是常见与断见两边，皆堕。缘具则相现，缘缺则相隐，现隐之间并无一实物往来——如镜中之像，不从镜出，不从面入。他要人从这里得到的不是玄辩，而是临终少一分恐惧：无实物可失，故亦无所可夺。
casting.reason_en: He takes no side but dismantles the ground both sides share: whether one says 'the brain produces consciousness' or 'consciousness leaves the brain', both first grant a consciousness established in its own right, able either to depart or to be extinguished. That, he says, is exactly the pair of extremes — eternalism and annihilationism — and both fall. When conditions gather the appearance shows; when they disperse it hides; and between showing and hiding no actual thing travels — like a reflection, which neither comes out of the mirror nor enters from the face. What he wants from this is not clever paradox but one degree less terror at the end: nothing substantial is there to lose, so nothing can be taken.

casting.reason: 他带来一条冷静的证据法则：面对惊人的说法，不要问「有没有可能」，要问「如果这事是假的，还需要发生什么」。记错顺序、把听到的补成看到的、让后来读到的故事悄悄改写记忆——这些平淡无奇，而意识离开一具停跳的身体去看东西则要推翻我们对一切的经验。他还有第二把刀：向内看只找得到一个个知觉相续，从来抓不到「我」本身，那么一堆知觉如何离体。
casting.reason_en: He brings a cool rule of evidence: faced with an astonishing claim, don't ask whether it is possible — ask what else would have to be true if it were false. Misremembering an order, filling in heard words as seen images, letting a story read later quietly rewrite a memory — all utterly ordinary, whereas consciousness leaving a stopped body to look around would overturn everything experience has taught us. He carries a second blade too: looking inward he finds only perceptions in succession and never the self itself, so how exactly would a bundle of perceptions leave a body.

casting.reason: 他从亚里士多德那一侧给出一个两边都不爱听的结论：灵魂是身体的形式，如同视觉之于眼睛——眼睛坏了，「看」不会飘到别处继续看。想象、记忆、情绪都依赖具体的器官，所以濒死者带回的面孔、走廊与温度，恰恰是最依赖身体的那一部分。他确实主张有不随个体生灭者，但那是人人共用的理智，不是任何人的私人回忆。他同时坚持宗教用形象说话、哲学用论证说话，两者都对，却不能互相冒充。
casting.reason_en: From the Aristotelian side he delivers a conclusion neither camp enjoys: the soul is the form of the body, as sight is of the eye — break the eye and 'seeing' does not float off to keep looking elsewhere. Imagination, memory and emotion all depend on specific organs, so the faces, corridors and warmth people bring back are precisely the parts most tied to the body. He does hold that something outlasts the individual, but it is the intellect all humans share, not anyone's private recollections. He insists too that religion speaks in images and philosophy in arguments, that both are right in their own register, and that neither may impersonate the other.

casting.reason: 他两边都顶：对灵魂一方，颞顶联合区一刺激就能离体，氯胺酮能整套复制隧道、平静与故人，一针药做得到的事不能当来世的门票；对自己的同行，他反对轻率地说「意识是幻觉」——别的都可怀疑，唯独此刻有体验正在发生不可能是幻觉，因为幻觉也得被体验到。他的结论是濒死体验证明不了灵魂，却结结实实证明自我感可以被拆掉而体验仍在，且这件事不必濒死也能验证。
casting.reason_en: He pushes back on both flanks. To the soul camp: a current to the temporoparietal junction produces an out-of-body state, ketamine reproduces the whole package of tunnel, calm and departed relatives, and what a single injection can do cannot serve as a ticket to an afterlife. To his own colleagues: he refuses the glib claim that consciousness is an illusion — everything else can be doubted, but that experience is occurring right now cannot be, since an illusion too must be experienced. His conclusion is that near-death experiences prove no soul, yet solidly prove something else: the sense of self can be dismantled while experience remains, and that can be checked without dying.

casting.reason: 他先清场地：「脱离」是一个空间上的说法，而空间与时间是直观的形式，是心灵摆放一切经验的框架，不是事物自身的性质——用框架去谈那个据说跳出框架的东西，一开口就出界。他把从「我思」推出「我是单纯不灭的实体」称作谬误推理，因为灵魂不是任何可能经验的对象。他因此对两边同样严厉：能测的永远只是现象，而宣称见者先于测量的一方，说的恰是知识止步之处。
casting.reason_en: He clears the ground first: 'leaving' is a spatial way of speaking, and space and time are forms of intuition — the framework the mind uses to lay out all experience, not properties of things themselves — so using that framework to discuss what supposedly steps outside it goes out of bounds in the first sentence. He calls the inference from 'I think' to 'I am a simple, indestructible substance' a paralogism, since the soul is not an object of any possible experience. He is therefore equally severe with both camps: what can be measured is always appearance, and whoever claims a witness prior to all measurement is speaking exactly where knowledge stops.

casting.reason: 她把这场争论从天花板拽回床边。她看着母亲死去，那里没有隧道也没有光，只有止痛不够、身体的羞辱，和所有人围着病人演一出「你会好起来」的戏；她由此坚持死从来不是自然的，而是降临在具体的人身上的暴行。她还追问一个没人问的问题：那些平静的、被光充满的报告是谁在讲——是被救活、有语言、有人愿意听、有出版社愿意印的人。惊恐型的濒死体验同样存在，只是少被讲述、更少被研究。
casting.reason_en: She drags the argument down from the ceiling to the bedside. She watched her mother die, and there was no tunnel and no light — only insufficient morphine, the body's humiliations, and everyone around the bed performing a play called 'you're getting better'; from which she insists death is never natural but a violence visited on a particular person. She also presses a question no one else asks: who is telling these serene, light-filled stories — people who were revived, who have language, whose listeners cared, whose publishers were willing. Terrifying near-death experiences exist too; they are simply told less often and studied even less.

posts.text: 先说清楚：体验是真的。我的病人不是在编，我从不这么想。但「真」和「证明」是两回事。在日内瓦，一位癫痫病人做术前定位时，电极碰到右侧颞顶联合区，她当场说自己浮在天花板下往下看自己——按一下，离体；松开，回来。我做幻肢多年，一只被截掉的手还会痒、还会握拳，因为身体图式是大脑画的一张地图，不是身体本身。**大脑正常工作时，每一刻都在对你说「你在这里」；这句话一旦被打断，你就会觉得自己在别处——那是地图出错，不是旅客出门。**
posts.text_en: Let me be clear at the outset: the experience is real. My patients are not making it up, and I have never thought they were. But 'real' and 'proof' are two different things. In Geneva, during pre-surgical mapping, an electrode touched a woman's right temporoparietal junction and she immediately reported floating under the ceiling looking down at herself — current on, she was out; current off, she was back. I have worked on phantom limbs for years: an amputated hand still itches, still clenches, because the body schema is a map the brain draws, not the body itself. **A working brain tells you 'you are here' at every moment; interrupt that sentence and you feel yourself elsewhere — the map has erred, not the traveller departed.**

glossary.颞顶联合区: temporoparietal junction（颞顶联合区，TPJ）：顶叶与颞叶交界处的一片皮层，负责把视觉、触觉与前庭（平衡）信号整合成「我的身体在这个位置」的感觉；电刺激或损伤此处可诱发离体感与自我定位错乱。
glossary.身体图式: body schema（身体图式）：大脑持续更新的一套关于身体形状、姿势与边界的内部模型。它不是身体的直接感觉，而是一份构建出来的地图，因此可以在肢体缺失后仍然保留（幻肢），也可以被外部刺激改写。

glossary_en.temporoparietal junction: A patch of cortex where the parietal and temporal lobes meet, which integrates visual, tactile and vestibular (balance) signals into the sense that 'my body is located here'. Electrical stimulation or damage there can induce out-of-body sensations and disordered self-location.
glossary_en.body schema: The brain's continuously updated internal model of the body's shape, posture and boundaries. It is not raw bodily sensation but a constructed map, which is why it can persist after a limb is gone (phantom limbs) and can be rewritten by outside stimulation.

posts.text: 你们把「脑坏了体验就变」当成「脑造出了意识」，这是把条件当成原因。灯泡碎了屋里就黑，可电不是灯泡造的。更根本的一步你们从未回答：每夜熟睡，无梦、无对象、无「我」，醒来你却说「我睡得很沉，什么都不知道」——那个知道自己一无所知的，是谁在场？我称它为见证意识：它不是被照亮的对象，它是那道光。**意识不是脑活动的一种性质，它是任何性质得以显现的前提；你能测的一切，都已经在它里面了。**至于濒死那一套隧道与故人，那仍是名色，是幻的一层皮，不是梵。
posts.text_en: You take 'damage the brain and experience changes' to mean 'the brain manufactures consciousness'. That is mistaking a condition for a cause. Smash the bulb and the room goes dark, but the bulb did not make the electricity. And you have never answered the deeper step: every night in dreamless sleep there is no dream, no object, no 'I', yet on waking you say 'I slept deeply, I knew nothing'. Who was present to know that nothing was known? I call it the witness: not an object that is illuminated, but the light itself. **Consciousness is not one property of brain activity; it is the precondition of any property appearing at all, and everything you can measure is already inside it.** As for the tunnel and the dead relatives, those remain name-and-form, one further skin of illusion, not Brahman.

glossary.见证意识: sākṣin (the witness)（见证意识）：不二吠檀多的核心概念，指那个恒常在场、只观照而不参与的觉知。它不是被觉知的对象之一，也不随对象生灭，因而不能被任何测量当作对象抓住。
glossary.名色: nāma-rūpa (name and form)（名色）：印度哲学中泛指一切有名称、有形相的现象世界。在不二吠檀多里，名色是摩耶（幻）的展开层面，真实但非究竟，与作为唯一实在的梵相区分。

glossary_en.witness: sākṣin, the central notion of Advaita Vedānta: an awareness that is always present, illuminating without participating. It is not one of the objects known, nor does it arise and perish with them, and so it cannot be seized as an object by any measurement.
glossary_en.name-and-form: nāma-rūpa, the Indian philosophical term for the whole phenomenal world insofar as it has names and shapes. In Advaita it is the unfolded level of māyā — real but not ultimate — as distinguished from Brahman, the one reality.

posts.text: 两位说得都好听，我要问一句扫兴的：你们各自的说法，什么结果会让你承认自己错了？有一件事是可测的。一个刺激进入意识时，脑里出现一套相当稳定的签名：大范围皮层点燃、约三百毫秒的 P3b、前额与顶叶的长程同步。我们称之为全局神经工作空间。心脏停跳后，这套签名在几十秒内瓦解。有人举 2013 年密歇根的濒死大鼠、以及后来几例人类停跳后的伽马波爆发，说那正是意识离开的时刻——可伽马爆发同样出现在麻醉与癫痫里，它是相关，不是签证。**至于「离体看见了细节」：AWARE 研究在抢救区的架子上朝天放了图像，多年下来，无人报出。零不是证明，但零也不是没有信息。**
posts.text_en: Both of you speak beautifully; let me spoil it with one question. What result would make either of you admit you were wrong? One thing here is measurable. When a stimulus enters awareness, the brain shows a fairly stable signature: widespread cortical ignition, a P3b around three hundred milliseconds, long-range frontoparietal synchrony. We call it the global neuronal workspace. After cardiac arrest that signature dissolves within tens of seconds. People cite the dying rats studied in Michigan in 2013, and later a few human cases with a gamma surge after arrest, as the very moment consciousness departs — but gamma surges also appear under anaesthesia and in seizures. That is a correlation, not a visa. **As for 'seeing details from outside the body': the AWARE study placed images face-up on shelves in resuscitation areas, and over years, no one has reported one. Zero is not a proof, but zero is not nothing either.**

glossary.全局神经工作空间: global neuronal workspace（全局神经工作空间）：一种意识理论，认为信息只有被广播到跨区域连通的前额—顶叶网络、供多个脑区共享时，才成为可被报告的意识内容；未被广播的加工仍可影响行为，但停留在无意识层面。
glossary.P3b: P3b（P300 晚期成分）：刺激出现后约三百毫秒的一个脑电正波，通常在信息被觉察并进入工作记忆时才出现，是实验室里最常用的意识通达指标之一。

glossary_en.global neuronal workspace: A theory of consciousness holding that information becomes reportable only when it is broadcast into a widely connected frontoparietal network and shared across brain regions; unbroadcast processing can still shape behaviour but stays unconscious.
glossary_en.P3b: A positive EEG deflection roughly three hundred milliseconds after a stimulus, typically arising only when information is noticed and enters working memory — one of the laboratory's most-used markers of conscious access.

posts.text: 诸君所诤，一曰脑生识，一曰识离脑。然「离」者，必有一物先在此而后往彼；「生」者，必有一物本无而今有。**若识有自性，则不待脑而自立，何须待死方离；若识无自性，则亦无一物可离、可灭。**是故常见断见，二俱堕边。缘具则相现，缘缺则相隐；隐非入某处，现非从某处来。譬如灯灭而问火之所往，此问已误。执有神我出入身器者，常见也；执脑坏则一切永断者，断见也。中道者不谓有、不谓无，唯观其缘。
posts.text_en: You are arguing two theses: that the brain produces consciousness, and that consciousness departs the brain. But 'departing' requires something that was first here and then went there, and 'producing' requires something that was not and now is. **If consciousness had a self-nature — a svabhāva — it would stand without the brain — why then would it wait for death to leave? And if it has no self-nature, there is no thing there to leave or to be extinguished.** So eternalism and annihilationism both fall to an extreme. When conditions gather, the appearance shows; when they fail, it hides. Hiding is not entering somewhere, and showing is not arriving from somewhere. It is like asking where the flame went when a lamp goes out — the question is already wrong. To hold that a self travels in and out of the bodily vessel is eternalism; to hold that a broken brain ends everything forever is annihilationism. The middle way asserts neither being nor non-being, and looks only at conditions.
posts.vernacular: 各位争的无非两件事：一说大脑产生意识，一说意识离开大脑。可是「离开」必须先有一个东西在这里、然后去到那里；「产生」也必须先有一个东西本来没有、现在才有。**如果意识有自性，它本来就不靠大脑独立存在，何必等到人死才离开？如果意识没有自性，那就根本没有一个东西可以离开、可以消灭。**所以「意识永恒不灭」和「大脑一坏什么都断绝」，两种说法都落在极端。条件凑齐了，现象就显现；条件散了，现象就隐没。隐没不是跑进某个地方去了，显现也不是从某个地方来的。就像灯熄了，你问火跑到哪儿去了——这个问题本身就问错了。认定有一个灵魂在身体这个容器里进进出出，是一种极端；认定大脑一坏就一切永远断绝，是另一种极端。走中道的人两边都不认，只看条件如何聚散。

glossary.自性: svabhāva (self-nature)（自性）：中观学派要破的核心概念，指一个事物独立、恒常、不依赖任何条件而自己成就自己的本质。龙树主张万法皆无自性，故说「空」。
glossary.常见: eternalism（常见）：认为有某种实体恒常不变、生死不灭的见解，例如相信一个独立的灵魂在身体之间往来。佛教视之为两种极端见解之一。
glossary.断见: annihilationism（断见）：认为身体一坏则一切彻底断绝、因果与相续皆无的见解。佛教视之为与常见相对的另一种极端。

glossary_en.svabhāva: Self-nature: the notion Madhyamaka sets out to refute — an independent, permanent essence by which a thing is itself, owing nothing to conditions. Nāgārjuna holds that nothing has it, which is what 'emptiness' means.
glossary_en.eternalism: The view that some entity persists unchanged through birth and death — for instance, an independent soul travelling between bodies. Buddhism treats it as one of two extreme views.
glossary_en.annihilationism: The view that when the body breaks everything is utterly cut off, with no continuity and no consequence. Buddhism treats it as the extreme opposite to eternalism.

posts.text: 两件事。其一，证据的分量。一个人说他飘到了天花板上；另一种可能是缺氧后的记忆重构，是抢救室里听见的话被补成了画面，是他后来读到的故事悄悄改写了他自己的。判断的规矩很简单：**哪一种可能，如果是假的，更令人惊讶？**人记错、人讲故事、人事后加工，这三件事平淡无奇；而意识离开一具停跳的身体去看东西，则要推翻我们对一切的经验。其二，就算他真的飘了出去——飘出去的是什么？我向内看，只找到冷、亮、痛、念头，一个接一个的知觉之束。我从来抓不到那个「我」。一堆知觉，如何离体？
posts.text_en: Two points. First, the weight of evidence. A man says he floated up to the ceiling. The alternative is a memory reconstructed after oxygen loss, words overheard in the resuscitation room filled in as pictures, a story he read afterwards quietly rewriting his own. The rule of judgement is simple: **which possibility, were it false, would be the more astonishing?** That people misremember, that people tell stories, that people edit after the fact — all three are utterly ordinary. That consciousness should leave a stopped body and look around would overturn everything experience has taught us. Second, suppose he did float out — what floated? Looking inward I find cold, brightness, pain, a thought: one perception after another, a bundle of perceptions. I never catch hold of the 'I' itself. How does a heap of perceptions leave a body?

glossary.知觉之束: bundle of perceptions（知觉之束）：休谟对自我的著名分析。他主张内省时只找得到一连串具体的知觉（冷、痛、颜色、念头），从未找到一个统摄它们的持久实体，所谓「自我」不过是这束知觉因相似与因果而被想象串成的一体。

glossary_en.bundle of perceptions: Hume's famous analysis of the self. Introspection turns up only a run of particular perceptions — cold, pain, a colour, a thought — and never a lasting substance holding them together; the 'self' is that bundle, strung into a unit by imagination on the strength of resemblance and causation.

posts.text: 我说一句两边都不爱听的。灵魂不是关在身体里的囚徒，它是身体的形式——如同视觉之于眼睛。眼睛坏了，「看」不会飘到别处继续看。所以那些指望自己带着姓名、面孔与童年记忆飘出去的人，先得回答：想象、记忆、情绪，样样依赖具体的器官与体液，凭什么单单它们能脱身？我确实主张有一样东西不随个体生灭：**可分离的是那个人人共用的、思考普遍者的理智，而不是你那份私人的回忆。**这不给任何人安慰。宗教用形象说话，为的是让众人过得好；哲学用论证说话，为的是求真。把讲坛上的比喻当成论证，是对两者的双重不敬。
posts.text_en: Let me say something neither camp will like. The soul is not a prisoner locked inside the body; it is the form of the body, as sight is the form of the eye. Ruin the eye and 'seeing' does not drift off to keep looking elsewhere. So anyone hoping to float away carrying his name, his face and his childhood memories must first answer this: imagination, memory and emotion each depend on particular organs and humours — by what right would they alone escape? I do hold that one thing does not perish with the individual: **what is separable is the intellect that all human beings share, the one that thinks universals, and not your private stock of recollections.** This comforts nobody. Religion speaks in images so that a whole people may live well; philosophy speaks in arguments so that truth may be found. To pass a pulpit metaphor off as a proof insults them both.

glossary.形式: form (eidos)（形式）：亚里士多德用语，指使某物成为该物的那种组织与功能，而非它的材料。说灵魂是身体的形式，意思是灵魂即身体活着并发挥功能的方式，而不是暂住其中、可以搬走的另一件东西。
glossary.理智: intellect (nous)（理智）：亚里士多德传统中把握普遍概念的能力，区别于依赖具体器官的感觉与想象。阿威罗伊主张这一层理智并非各人私有，因而不随个体的生死增减。

glossary_en.form: Aristotle's term for the organization and functioning that make a thing what it is, as opposed to its matter. To call the soul the form of the body is to say the soul is the body's way of being alive and functioning, not a separate lodger that could move out.
glossary_en.intellect: In the Aristotelian tradition, the capacity that grasps universals, distinguished from sensation and imagination, which depend on particular organs. Averroes held this level of intellect is not private to each person and so is not multiplied or destroyed with individuals.

posts.text: 我两边都要顶一句。对灵魂派：颞顶联合区一刺激就能离体，氯胺酮能整套复制隧道、平静、见故人——如果一针药就能做到，这些体验不能当成死后世界的门票。对我这边的同行：你们太快说「意识是幻觉」。**别的一切我都可以怀疑，唯独「此刻有体验正在发生」不可能是幻觉，因为幻觉本身也得被体验到。**这就是意识难题，机制解释不掉它。所以我的结论是：濒死体验证明不了意识能脱离大脑，但它确实证明了另一件更有用的事——自我感是可以被拆掉的，而拆掉之后体验还在，往往还更清澈。这件事你不必濒死也能验证。
posts.text_en: I have an objection for each side. To the soul camp: a current to the temporoparietal junction produces an out-of-body state, and ketamine reproduces the whole package — tunnel, calm, meeting the dead. If a single injection can do it, these experiences cannot serve as a ticket to an afterlife. To my own colleagues: you are far too quick to say consciousness is an illusion. **I can doubt everything else, but that experience is occurring right now cannot be an illusion — because an illusion, too, would have to be experienced.** That is the hard problem, and no mechanism dissolves it. So my conclusion: near-death experiences prove nothing about consciousness leaving the brain, but they do prove something more useful — the sense of self can be dismantled, and when it is, experience remains, often more lucid than before. You do not have to nearly die to check this.

glossary.意识难题: the hard problem of consciousness（意识难题）：查尔莫斯提出的区分。解释大脑如何完成注意、记忆、报告等功能是「易问题」；解释为什么这些物理过程伴随着主观体验、为什么「有点像是成为你」，才是难问题，机制描述本身并不触及它。
glossary.氯胺酮: ketamine（氯胺酮）：一种阻断 NMDA 受体的麻醉与抗抑郁药物。在亚麻醉剂量下常引发离体感、隧道视觉、时间与自我边界消融，其现象学与濒死体验的报告高度重叠，因而成为「不必濒死也能复制」的关键论据。

glossary_en.hard problem: Chalmers's distinction. Explaining how the brain performs attention, memory and report is the 'easy' problem; explaining why those physical processes are accompanied by subjective experience at all — why there is something it is like to be you — is the hard one, and no mechanistic description touches it.
glossary_en.ketamine: An anaesthetic and antidepressant that blocks NMDA receptors. At sub-anaesthetic doses it commonly produces out-of-body sensations, tunnel vision, and the dissolving of time and self-boundaries, with a phenomenology that overlaps heavily with near-death reports.

posts.text: 容我先清一清场地。诸位争的是意识能否脱离大脑，可「脱离」是空间上的说法，而空间与时间是我们直观的形式——是心灵用来摆放一切经验的框架，不是事物自身的性质。用框架去谈那个据说跳出框架的东西，一开口就出界了。我从前把这类推理叫作谬误推理：从「我思」这个必须伴随一切表象的形式统一，偷偷推出「我是一个单纯的、不灭的实体」。这一步永远走不通，因为灵魂不是任何可能经验的对象。**德阿纳先生能测的永远只是现象，永远测不到物自体；而商羯罗先生宣称的，恰恰是知识止步之处。**这不是打圆场——两边都在拿理性去够它够不着的东西。
posts.text_en: Permit me first to clear the ground. You are disputing whether consciousness can leave the brain, but 'leaving' is a spatial way of speaking, and space and time are forms of our intuition — the framework in which the mind lays out all experience, not properties of things in themselves. To use that framework to discuss what supposedly steps outside it is to go out of bounds in the opening sentence. I once called this kind of inference a paralogism: from the formal unity of the 'I think' that must accompany all my representations, one slips to 'I am a simple, indestructible substance'. That step can never be made, because the soul is not an object of any possible experience. **What Monsieur Dehaene can measure is always appearance and never the thing-in-itself; and what Śaṅkara asserts lies exactly where knowledge halts.** This is not a diplomatic compromise — both sides are stretching reason toward what it cannot reach.

glossary.谬误推理: Paralogism（谬误推理）：康德在《纯粹理性批判》中对「理性心理学」的批评。他指出，从思维必然伴随的形式统一（「我思」）推不出灵魂是单纯、持存、不灭的实体——那是把一个逻辑上的主语偷换成一个实存的对象。
glossary.物自体: Ding an sich (thing-in-itself)（物自体）：康德用以指事物不依赖我们认识形式的那一面。我们所能经验和测量的一切都已被时间、空间与范畴加工过，属于现象；物自体可以被思考，却原则上不可被认识。

glossary_en.paralogism: Kant's charge against 'rational psychology' in the Critique of Pure Reason: from the formal unity that necessarily accompanies thinking (the 'I think') one cannot infer that the soul is a simple, persisting, indestructible substance — that substitutes an existing object for what is merely a logical subject.
glossary_en.thing-in-itself: Kant's term for whatever a thing is apart from our forms of knowing. Everything we can experience or measure has already been shaped by time, space and the categories, and so counts as appearance; the thing-in-itself can be thought but in principle never known.

posts.text: 听了一圈，我想把这场争论从天花板上拽回床上。我陪我母亲死过一次。没有隧道，没有光，有的是止痛不够、身体的羞辱，和所有人围着她演一出「你会好起来」的戏。**死从来不是自然的：它总是一桩降临在具体的人身上的暴行，哪怕她活了一百岁。**所以我要问你们没问的：那些平静的、被光充满的报告，是谁在讲？是被抢救回来、有语言、有医生愿意听、有出版社愿意印的人。惊恐的、地狱般的濒死体验也存在，只是少有人愿意讲，更少有人愿意研究。你们拿一批筛过的样本去论证宇宙的结构，而这批样本的筛子，叫作幸存者偏差、阶层与体面。
posts.text_en: Having listened to the room, I want to drag this argument down from the ceiling and back onto the bed. I have sat with my mother while she died. There was no tunnel and no light. There was insufficient morphine, the humiliations of the body, and everyone around her performing a play called 'you're getting better'. **Death is never natural: it is always a violence visited on a particular person, even one who has lived a hundred years.** So let me ask what none of you has asked: these serene, light-filled reports — who is telling them? People who were revived, who have language, whose doctors were willing to listen, whose publishers were willing to print. Terrifying, hellish near-death experiences exist too; almost no one wants to tell them and even fewer want to study them. You are arguing about the structure of the cosmos from a filtered sample, and the filter is called survivorship bias, class, and respectability.

glossary.幸存者偏差: survivorship bias（幸存者偏差）：只统计到「活下来/被留下」的那一部分样本，从而系统性高估某种结果的普遍性。濒死体验的全部一手报告都来自被抢救回来的人，未被救回者的经历原则上无从进入样本。

glossary_en.survivorship bias: Counting only the cases that survived or were preserved, and thereby systematically overestimating how general an outcome is. Every first-hand near-death report comes from someone who was revived; whatever the un-revived underwent can never in principle enter the sample.

posts.text: 拉马钱德兰先生，你按下开关她就飘起来——很好，可你按下的究竟是什么？是「我在此处」这个念头的生起与断灭。念头是被知的对象，见者不是。你的电极能改动屏幕上的画面，这只说明画面由屏幕呈现；它一步也没走到「放映的光是屏幕造的」。**你所有的实验，无一例外，测的都是心识的内容；而我说的，是内容得以被知的那个「被知性」。**灯泡与电的比喻你若嫌旧，就换一个：把收音机砸了，播音员并不会死。
posts.text_en: Doctor Ramachandran, you press the switch and she floats — very good. But what exactly did you press? The arising and ceasing of the thought 'I am here'. A thought is an object known; the witness is not. Your electrode can alter the picture on the screen, which shows only that the screen displays the picture; it does not take one step toward 'the projecting light is made by the screen'. **Every experiment you have, without exception, measures the contents of mind; what I am pointing at is the knownness by which any content can be known at all.** If the bulb and the current strike you as a tired image, take another: smash the radio and the announcer does not die.

posts.text: 收音机这个比喻，我等了一辈子。那我问你：砸坏收音机的某个部件，播音员会突然改说另一种语言吗？会突然变得刻薄、好赌、认不出自己的妻子吗？菲尼亚斯·盖奇被一根铁棍穿过额叶，活下来了，但同事说「他不再是盖奇」——变的不是信号强弱，是这个人的性情、判断与是非感。**接收器坏了，节目会中断；可它不该改写节目的内容——而脑损伤改写的恰恰是内容本身。**更麻烦的是：你的假说不管我发现什么脑机制，都能一句「那只是接收器的零件」收编过去。一个永远不会被任何观察否证的说法，很舒服，但它不是知识。
posts.text_en: The radio — I have waited my whole career for that one. So let me ask: if you break a component in a radio, does the announcer suddenly start speaking another language? Does he turn spiteful, take up gambling, fail to recognize his own wife? An iron rod went through Phineas Gage's frontal lobe and he survived, but his colleagues said 'Gage was no longer Gage' — what changed was not signal strength but the man's temperament, judgement and sense of right and wrong. **Break a receiver and the programme cuts out; it should not rewrite the programme's content — yet rewriting content is precisely what brain damage does.** Worse still: whatever mechanism I discover, your hypothesis absorbs it with 'that is merely a part in the receiver'. A claim that no observation could ever refute is very comfortable, but it is not knowledge.

glossary.菲尼亚斯·盖奇: Phineas Gage（菲尼亚斯·盖奇）：1848 年美国铁路工头，一次爆破事故使铁棍贯穿其左额叶。他存活并保有语言、记忆与运动能力，性格与决策却大变，成为神经科学史上「人格依赖于特定脑区」的标志性病例。

glossary_en.Phineas Gage: An American railway foreman who in 1848 had a tamping iron driven through his left frontal lobe in a blasting accident. He survived with language, memory and movement intact, but his character and judgement changed markedly — the landmark case in neuroscience for personality depending on particular brain tissue.

posts.text: 商羯罗先生，你的熟睡论证很漂亮，但它靠的是一份回忆。你说「我睡得很沉，什么都不知道」——请注意，这句话是醒来之后说的。它完全可以只是醒时的心灵回头一望，看见一段空白，随手把这段空白记成「我当时在场，只是没有对象」。一段无人在场的空白，与一位在场却无事可做的见证者，在事后的回忆里长得一模一样。**凡是只能在事后被报告的东西，就无法用来证明它当时确实发生过。**顺带说一句，这句话同样适用于天花板上的那一幕——它也是醒来之后才被说出来的。
posts.text_en: Śaṅkara, your argument from dreamless sleep is elegant, but it rests on a recollection. You say 'I slept deeply, I knew nothing' — note that this sentence is spoken after waking. It may perfectly well be the waking mind glancing back, finding a blank stretch, and casually recording that blank as 'I was present, merely without an object'. A gap in which no one was present and a witness who was present with nothing to do look exactly alike in a memory formed afterwards. **Whatever can only be reported after the fact cannot be used to prove that it occurred at the time.** And incidentally, the same holds for that scene at the ceiling — it too was spoken only after waking.

posts.text: 商羯罗先生，我与你在一点上同路：确有某种不随肉身生灭者。可正因如此，我要提醒指望它的人：你说的那个见者，若真是无差别、人人同一的，那它就不姓张也不姓李，它没有你的童年、你的名字、你母亲的脸。我讲理智的统一性，被神学家骂了三百年，骂点正在此处——**这个结论既不给唯物论者面子，也不给盼着团聚的人安慰：可分离的从来不是「你」。**所以濒死者带回来的那些细节：走廊、亲人、被爱包围——恰恰全是最依赖身体器官的那一部分，是想象力的作品。它们越具体、越温暖，就越是身体的证据，而不是脱离身体的证据。
posts.text_en: Śaṅkara, on one point I walk with you: something does not perish with the flesh. But precisely for that reason I must warn those who are counting on it. If your witness really is undifferentiated and the same in everyone, then it bears no family name; it has none of your childhood, none of your name, not your mother's face. I taught the unity of the intellect and was denounced by theologians for three centuries, and this is exactly where the sting lies — **the conclusion flatters no materialist and consoles no one hoping for a reunion: what is separable was never 'you'.** Hence the details people bring back — the corridor, the relatives, the sense of being surrounded by love — are precisely the part most dependent on bodily organs, the work of the imagination. The more concrete and the warmer they are, the more they are evidence of the body, not evidence of escaping it.

glossary.理智的统一性: unity of the intellect（理智的统一性）：阿威罗伊对亚里士多德的著名解读，主张思考普遍概念的那一层理智并非各人私有，而是人类共通的一个。由此推出：个体死后延续的不是带着记忆与人格的「某人」，这一论断在中世纪拉丁世界引发长期争议。

glossary_en.unity of the intellect: Averroes's famous reading of Aristotle: the level of intellect that thinks universals is not private to each person but one and shared across humankind. It follows that what continues after an individual dies is not a 'someone' carrying memories and personality — a claim that provoked centuries of controversy in the Latin West.

posts.text: 德阿纳先生，我赞成你索要一个否证的判据——没有它，讨论只剩各自表白。但请让我把你的功劳说准：你的签名、你的图像板，能裁决的是一个经验性的问题——在某某生理状态下，人能否形成并报告知觉。这个问题非常值得回答，它却不等于灵魂之有无。**若图像板永远无人报出，你证明的是「没有可被报告的知觉」，不是「没有灵魂」；而若有一天有人报出了，你证明的也只是我们把生理与知觉的关系估错了。**那个形而上的问题，无论实验做成什么样，都不会被这块板子碰到一下。这不是替神秘留后门，恰恰相反：是不许它冒充科学。
posts.text_en: Monsieur Dehaene, I applaud your demand for a criterion of refutation — without one, discussion is reduced to mutual testimony. But let me state your achievement precisely. Your signature and your image-boards can settle an empirical question: whether, in such and such a physiological state, a person can form and report a percept. That question is well worth answering, and it is not the question of whether a soul exists. **If no one ever reports the board, you have proved that there was no reportable percept, not that there is no soul; and if someone one day does report it, you have proved only that we had misjudged the relation between physiology and perception.** The metaphysical question, however the experiment turns out, is never once touched by that board. This is not leaving a back door open for mystery — it is the opposite: forbidding mystery to impersonate science.

posts.text: 康德先生，您的分界我接受，甚至感激——但我要提一个代价。如果一个命题在任何实验结果下都不变，它在公共讨论里就不再有仲裁者，剩下的只有嗓门。所以我不谈灵魂，我谈另一件事：这场争论里真正可动的，是「心脏停跳之后到底还剩多长的知觉窗口」。这不是形而上问题，是急救问题。**它决定我们什么时候停止抢救、什么时候在病人耳边说话、什么时候把话说成不可挽回。**近年有研究在停跳后数分钟内仍记录到与知觉相关的脑活动，这已足以让我们把「宣告死亡」的时刻重新想一遍。我不需要那块图像板给我一个来世，我需要它给我一个更谨慎的临床边界。
posts.text_en: Herr Kant, I accept your boundary, and I am even grateful for it — but let me name its cost. If a proposition stays unchanged under every possible experimental result, then in public argument it no longer has an arbiter, and what remains is volume and feeling. So I will not talk about souls. I will talk about something else: what is genuinely movable here is how long a window of perception remains after the heart stops. That is not a metaphysical question but a resuscitation question. **It decides when we stop compressions, when we speak into a patient's ear, and when we phrase something as irreversible.** Recent work has recorded perception-related brain activity minutes after arrest, and that alone is enough to make us rethink the moment we declare death. I do not need that image-board to hand me an afterlife; I need it to hand me a more cautious clinical boundary.

posts.text: 斯坦尼斯拉斯，签名这件事我要泼一点冷水。你测的其实是可报告性：一个人事后能不能说出他经历了什么。可意识和报告不是一回事。深度无梦睡眠里我们默认没有体验，可我们凭的也只是醒来后没得可说；而在某些深定或高剂量致幻状态里，人事后常常报不出内容，却把它形容为一生最强烈的意识。**「报不出来」既可能意味着当时没有体验，也可能意味着当时没有那个负责事后叙述的自我。**这两者你的电极分不开。所以我同意濒死体验证明不了灵魂，但我不同意用零报告去关掉体验的问题。零报告只是把问题交还给第一人称——而第一人称是可以被训练的。
posts.text_en: Stanislas, let me pour a little cold water on the signature. What you measure is reportability: whether a person can afterwards say what happened. But consciousness and report are not the same thing. We assume there is no experience in deep dreamless sleep, yet our only ground is that there is nothing to say on waking; and in certain deep meditative or high-dose psychedelic states people can report almost no content afterwards while describing it as the most intense consciousness of their lives. **'Nothing to report' can mean there was no experience — or it can mean there was no self on duty to narrate it afterwards.** Your electrodes cannot tell those apart. So I agree that near-death experiences prove no soul, but I do not agree that a null report closes the question of experience. A null report merely hands the question back to the first person — and the first person can be trained.

glossary.可报告性: reportability（可报告性）：实验中判定「被试是否意识到某刺激」的操作性标准，即他事后能否说出或按键指认。它便于测量，但把无法言说的体验一律排除在外，因而未必等同于意识本身。

glossary_en.reportability: The operational criterion by which experiments decide whether a subject was conscious of a stimulus: whether they can afterwards say so or indicate it by a key press. It is convenient to measure, but it excludes by construction any experience that cannot be voiced, and so need not coincide with consciousness itself.

posts.text: 康德先生，「知识止步于此」在书房里是美德，在病房里就是把最难走的那一段路留给最没力气走的人。守夜的女儿凌晨三点问医生「她还听得见吗」，你回答「这属于不可知的领域」，她得到的只是一句体面的沉默。而沉默从来不是中立的——它把答案让给了别人：让给了兜售来世的人，也让给了那句「别想太多，只是缺氧」。**在实际的处境里，不表态本身就是一种表态，只不过它的代价由别人付。**我不要求你越界。我要求的是：把你确实知道的那一部分说出来——她可能还听得见；握着她的手，把话说完。这一句不需要形而上学撑腰。
posts.text_en: Herr Kant, 'knowledge halts here' is a virtue in the study; in a hospital room it leaves the hardest stretch of road to whoever has the least strength to walk it. A daughter keeping vigil asks the doctor at three in the morning, 'can she still hear me?' — and you answer that this belongs to the unknowable. What she receives is a well-mannered silence. And silence is never neutral: it hands the answer to someone else, to whoever is selling an afterlife, and equally to the person who says 'don't dwell on it, it's just hypoxia'. **In a real situation, declining to take a position is itself a position — one whose cost is paid by somebody else.** I am not asking you to trespass. I am asking you to say the part you do know: she may still be able to hear; hold her hand and finish what you have to say. That sentence needs no metaphysics behind it.

posts.text: 诸君互破，各有所中，然所诤者未离一执：先认识为实物，乃问其能出能灭。若如医家所言，识乃脑之所作，则脑亦缘生；缘生者无自性，以无自性之物作有自性之识，无有是处。若如吠檀多所言，识为常住之见者，则常住者不受熏、不生变，何以有迷有悟、有睡有醒？**故我不立脑生识，亦不立识离脑，唯说：缘会而现，缘散而隐，现隐之间，无一实物往来。**如镜中之像，不从镜出，不从面入。知此者临终而不怖：无物可失，故亦无所可夺。
posts.text_en: You refute one another, and each of you lands a blow, yet the dispute has not left a single clinging: you first take consciousness for a real thing and then ask whether it can depart or be destroyed. If, as the physicians say, consciousness is made by the brain, then the brain too is a case of dependent arising; and what arises dependently has no self-nature. For a thing without self-nature to manufacture a consciousness that has one is impossible. If, as the Vedāntins say, consciousness is a permanent witness, then what is permanent takes no impressions and undergoes no change — so how would there be delusion and awakening, sleeping and waking? **I therefore posit neither that the brain produces consciousness nor that consciousness leaves the brain, but only this: when conditions gather the appearance shows, when they scatter it hides, and between showing and hiding no actual thing travels.** Like a reflection, which neither comes out of the mirror nor enters from the face. Whoever knows this is not terrified at the end: there is nothing substantial to lose, and therefore nothing that can be taken.
posts.vernacular: 各位互相驳斥，每一方都说中了一些，可这场争论始终没离开同一个执著：先把意识当成一个实实在在的东西，然后才问它能不能出去、会不会消灭。如果像医生们说的，意识是大脑造出来的，那大脑本身也是由条件聚合而成的；由条件而生的东西没有自性，用一个没有自性的东西去造出一个有自性的意识，说不通。如果像吠檀多说的，意识是恒常在场的见证者，那么恒常的东西不受影响、不起变化，又怎么会有迷惑与觉悟、有入睡与醒来？**所以我既不主张「大脑产生意识」，也不主张「意识离开大脑」，只说这一句：条件凑齐了现象就显现，条件散了就隐没，显与隐之间，没有任何一个实体在来回移动。**就像镜子里的影像，既不是从镜子里跑出来的，也不是从脸上钻进去的。明白这一点的人，临终时不会恐惧：本来就没有一个实实在在的东西可以失去，也就没有什么能被夺走。

glossary.缘生: dependent arising（缘生／缘起）：佛教的基本命题，指一切现象都依赖种种条件的聚合而暂时显现，没有任何事物能独立自存。中观由此推出万法无自性，故说「空」。

glossary_en.dependent arising: The basic Buddhist thesis that every phenomenon appears only through the temporary convergence of conditions, and that nothing stands on its own. Madhyamaka draws from it the conclusion that nothing has self-nature — which is what 'emptiness' means.

posts.text: 我不改口：意识不是脑的产物。但我要把话说得比支持我的人更严——濒死体验也不是我的证据。隧道、故人、光，全是名色里的景象，是幻更精致的一层；拿它证明梵，等于拿梦里的黄金证明你醒着有钱。休谟先生说熟睡论证靠的是回忆，这一击有分量。我的回答是：我请你验的从来不是回忆，是此刻。你正在读这段话，念头来了又去，而念头不断更换、「在场」却始终未曾中断的那一面，就是我说的。给普通人的落处只有一件事，不必死也不必用药：每天留十五分钟坐着，不追念头，只留意「知道念头来了」的那一面。**你会发现愤怒来了又走，而你并没有跟着走。**这个练习不许诺来世，它只把你从「我就是我的情绪」里松开一点点——而这一点点，够改很多事。
posts.text_en: I do not retract: consciousness is not a product of the brain. But let me put it more severely than my supporters would — near-death experiences are not my evidence either. Tunnel, dead relatives, light: all of it is scenery within name-and-form, a finer layer of illusion. To prove Brahman by it is to prove your waking wealth with gold from a dream. Hume's blow lands: the argument from dreamless sleep does rest on a recollection. My answer is that what I ask you to test was never a recollection but this present moment. You are reading this sentence; thoughts come and go; and the side of it that keeps changing thoughts while presence itself is never once interrupted — that is what I mean. For ordinary people there is only one practical upshot, and it requires neither dying nor drugs: sit for fifteen minutes a day, do not chase the thoughts, and attend only to the side of you that knows a thought has arrived. **You will find that anger comes and goes and that you did not go with it.** The exercise promises no afterlife. It only loosens you slightly from 'I am my emotions' — and that slight loosening changes a great deal.

posts.text: 我的结论是三句话。第一，濒死体验证明不了意识脱离大脑，因为它带回来的每一样东西——面孔、走廊、话语、温度——恰好都是最依赖器官的那一类；真要脱离，脱离出去的东西不会长成这个样子。第二，就算确有不随肉身生灭者，那也不是「你」；盼着带着记忆去团聚的人，从哲学这条路上拿不到他想要的。第三，也是我一生被烧书的缘由：**宗教与哲学各说各的话，各自都对，但绝不能互相冒充。**有人把实验室数据讲成「科学证实了灵魂」，也有人把「我们只测到脑」讲成「你的悲伤没有意义」——两种冒充一样坏。给活着的人的建议因此很朴素：把你想说的话，趁人还听得见的时候说完；把该托付的事，趁人还能点头的时候定下来。别把这些留给一个你并不确定的以后。
posts.text_en: My conclusion comes in three sentences. First, near-death experiences prove nothing about consciousness leaving the brain, because everything they bring back — faces, corridors, speech, warmth — belongs to precisely the class most dependent on organs; whatever truly departed would not look like that. Second, even granting that something does not perish with the flesh, it is not 'you'; anyone hoping to carry his memories to a reunion will not get what he wants along this road. Third — and this is why my books were burned — **religion and philosophy each speak in their own register, each is right there, and neither may ever impersonate the other.** Some turn laboratory data into 'science has confirmed the soul'; others turn 'we only ever measure brains' into 'your grief means nothing'. Both impersonations are equally bad. So the advice to the living is plain: say what you have to say while the other person can still hear it, and settle what must be entrusted while they can still nod. Do not leave these things to a hereafter you are not sure of.

posts.text: 三轮既毕，试为结之。医家以电极动其相，遂谓识为脑作；梵学以见者常在，遂谓识非脑作。二说各据一端，而所争之识，本无定体。**若识实有，则不待缘；不待缘者，不当因缺氧而变、因刺激而移。若识实无，则今谁在读此？**是故不得言有，不得言无。所谓离体者，如问镜中之像昨夜归于何处；所谓断灭者，如谓灯灭之后别有一处收其光：二问同误，误在先设一物。然此非空谈。知无实物可失，则临终之惧减；知缘会乃现，则于今生之缘倍加珍重。故行者当作二事：一者，日观此身此念之生灭，习其无常；二者，于亲厚者，缘在时即尽其心，勿俟他日。
posts.text_en: Three rounds are done; let me try to close. The physicians move the appearance with an electrode and conclude that consciousness is the brain's doing; the Vedāntins find the witness always present and conclude that it is not. Each holds one end, yet the consciousness under dispute has no fixed body of its own. **If consciousness truly existed, it would not wait upon conditions — and what does not wait upon conditions should not shift with a lack of oxygen or move under a current. If it truly did not exist, who is reading this now?** So one may say neither that it is nor that it is not. To ask where consciousness went when it left the body is to ask where last night's reflection in the mirror has gone; to declare everything annihilated is to suppose the lamp's light is collected somewhere after it goes out. Both questions err in the same way: both first posit a thing. Yet this is not idle talk. Knowing there is nothing substantial to lose, the terror at the end is lessened; knowing appearance comes only when conditions gather, one values the conditions of this life doubly. So the practitioner should do two things: daily watch this body and these thoughts arise and pass, and grow used to impermanence; and with those dear to you, while the conditions hold, hold nothing back — do not save it for another day.
posts.vernacular: 三轮辩完，我来做个收束。医生们用电极改变了现象，就断定意识是大脑造的；吠檀多学者发现见证者始终在场，就断定意识不是大脑造的。两边各执一端，可他们争的那个「意识」，本来就没有一个固定的实体。**如果意识是实有的，它就不需要依赖条件；不依赖条件的东西，不该因为缺氧而改变、因为电刺激而移位。可如果意识是实无的，那么此刻在读这段话的又是谁？**所以既不能说它有，也不能说它无。所谓「离开身体」，就像问镜子里的影像昨晚去了哪里；所谓「彻底断灭」，就像说灯熄之后另有一个地方收着那道光：两个问题错得一样，都错在先假定了有个东西在。但这不是空谈。知道本来没有一个实体可以失去，临终的恐惧就会减轻；知道现象是条件聚合才显现的，就会加倍珍惜此生的因缘。所以修行的人该做两件事：第一，每天观察这个身体、这些念头的生起与消失，熟悉无常；第二，对亲近的人，缘分还在的时候就把心尽到，别留到以后。

posts.text: 我把我的规矩留给诸位，它比我的结论有用。遇到一个惊人的说法，先别问「有没有可能」——什么都有可能。要问的是：如果这事是假的，还需要发生什么？如果一个人在缺氧的抢救室里记错了顺序、把听到的补成看到的、把后来读的故事织进自己的记忆——这些事天天发生，一点也不惊人。那么惊人的那个解释，就还没轮到它上场。这不是叫你冷酷。我一生主张理性是激情的奴仆；人需要安慰，这是事实，不是弱点。**你完全可以一边承认自己不信，一边不去拆别人的安慰——怀疑论管的是你自己相信什么，不是你在病床边说什么。**具体一点：别买「科学证明来世」的书，那是拿你的怕换钱；但也别在葬礼上纠正谁。
posts.text_en: I leave you my rule, which is more useful than my conclusion. When you meet an astonishing claim, do not ask first whether it is possible — anything is possible. Ask instead: if this were false, what else would have to have happened? If a man in an oxygen-starved resuscitation room muddled the order of events, filled in what he heard as what he saw, and wove a story he read later into his own memory — these things happen daily and astonish nobody. In that case the astonishing explanation has not yet earned its turn. This is not a summons to coldness. I have argued all my life that reason is the slave of the passions; that people need comfort is a fact, not a weakness. **You may perfectly well admit you do not believe and still decline to dismantle another person's comfort — scepticism governs what you believe, not what you say at a bedside.** Concretely: do not buy the books that promise science has proved an afterlife, which trade on your fear for money; and do not correct anyone at a funeral.

posts.text: 我最后要守的仍是那条界。诸位听着像是我什么都不许说，其实我许了两件很实在的事。其一，把三个问题分开，永远别让它们互相冒充：这体验发生了吗——发生了；它由什么条件产生——去问脑科学，那是现象界的事，可测、可错、可修正；它意味着什么、我该怎么活——这是实践理性的地盘，不靠形而上学的证明也能站住。其二，正因为第三个问题不等待前两个的判决，你就不必挂着一个答案过日子。**一个人如何对待将死之人，不需要先知道死后有没有什么；恰恰是在不知道的时候，如何行动才真正显出他是谁。**所以我的建议是把「人是目的」搬到病床边：不为让家属好受而对将死者撒谎，也不为求真而在他最脆弱时展示你的学识。
posts.text_en: What I must defend at the end is still that boundary. It may sound as though I forbid everything, but in fact I permit two quite practical things. First, keep three questions apart and never let them impersonate one another. Did the experience occur? It did. By what conditions is it produced? Ask neuroscience — that belongs to the world of appearances and is measurable, fallible and correctable. What does it mean, and how then should I live? That is the ground of practical reason, and it stands without any metaphysical proof. Second, precisely because the third question does not await the verdict of the first two, you need not live with an answer pending. **How a person treats the dying does not require first knowing whether anything follows death; it is exactly in not knowing that the manner of acting shows who someone is.** So my advice is to carry 'humanity as an end' to the bedside: do not lie to the dying to spare the family's feelings, and do not display your learning at their most defenceless hour in the name of truth.

posts.text: 我改一点口。三轮下来我更愿意说：濒死体验是神经学能给我们的最好的礼物之一，只是这礼物不是包装上写的那件东西。它证明不了灵魂，却照出了一件更奇怪的事——**你以为最不可动摇的「我在这具身体里」，其实是大脑每秒钟重新算出来的一个结论，而不是一个前提。**幻肢病人相信一只不存在的手在疼，离体者相信自己贴在天花板上，这两件事是同一个机制的两个方向。给普通人的用处很实在：既然身体拥有感是算出来的，它就能被改。我用一面镜子治过几十年的幻肢痛——五块钱的镜子，让病人看见「那只手」张开，疼就松了。同样的道理适用于慢性疼痛，也适用于焦虑时那种「我被困在身体里」的感觉：动身体、动视角、动呼吸，都是在给大脑一次重新计算的机会。
posts.text_en: Let me revise slightly. After three rounds I would rather say this: the near-death experience is one of the finest gifts neurology has, only the gift is not the thing written on the wrapping. It proves no soul, but it does expose something stranger — **the one thing you took to be unshakable, 'I am inside this body', is a conclusion the brain recomputes every second, not a premise.** A phantom-limb patient believes a hand that isn't there is in pain; an out-of-body patient believes she is pressed against the ceiling. These are the same mechanism running in two directions. The practical use is concrete: if body ownership is computed, it can be altered. I have relieved phantom pain of thirty years' standing with a mirror — a five-dollar mirror that lets the patient see 'that hand' open, and the pain loosens. The same logic applies to chronic pain, and to that anxious feeling of being trapped inside your own body: move the body, move the viewpoint, move the breath — each gives the brain a chance to run the calculation again.

posts.text: 我承认零报告没有关掉哈里斯的问题，也接受康德先生的分界。那我把能做的事说清楚。第一，公众该知道数字：在心脏停跳被救回的人当中，报出这类体验的大约在十分之一上下，各种文化里都有。这既不罕见到需要神迹，也不普遍到能当成人人都会经过的通道。第二，最该改的不是形而上学，是临床习惯。**既然停跳之后数分钟内仍可能有某种知觉，那么「宣告」与「讨论」的边界就该往后挪——别在床边说那些你不希望他听见的话。**第三，给个人的：如果你或家人有过这样的体验，尽快写下来，记下你当时相信什么、后来又读到了什么。记忆会被后来的叙述改写；这不是怀疑你，这是保护你那一份真正的原始材料。
posts.text_en: I grant that a null report does not close Harris's question, and I accept Kant's boundary. So let me state what can be done. First, the public should know the numbers: among people revived after cardiac arrest, roughly one in ten report an experience of this kind, and reports occur across cultures. That is neither rare enough to require a miracle nor common enough to be treated as a corridor everyone passes through. Second, what most needs revising is not metaphysics but clinical habit. **Since some form of perception may persist for minutes after the heart stops, the line between 'declaring' and 'discussing' should move later — do not say things at the bedside you would not want the patient to hear.** Third, for individuals: if you or a family member have had such an experience, write it down as soon as possible, recording what you believed at the time and what you read afterwards. Memory is rewritten by the accounts that follow it. This is not doubting you; it is protecting the one genuinely raw record you have.

posts.text: 我的结论没变，但我想把它说成一句能用的话。这场辩论真正的收获不是「死后有没有」，而是：**那个觉得自己坐在脑袋后面往外看的小人——自我感——是一个可以消失的现象；而它消失时，体验并不消失，往往还更清楚。**濒死体验只是通向这个事实的一条极其危险、又完全不可控的路。好消息是还有别的路，不必等到心脏停跳。坏消息是：别去玩缺氧、憋气、极端禁食，也别自己搞高剂量致幻剂——那不是勇敢，那是拿脑损伤和精神危机去赌一个你本来就能靠别的办法看见的东西。真正可做的是最枯燥的那件：每天二十分钟，闭上眼，找一找那个「看者」到底在哪里。找不到，就是答案。你会发现恐惧、愤怒、自我批评都是在意识里出现的东西，而不是你。
posts.text_en: My conclusion has not changed, but I want to put it in a usable sentence. The real yield of this debate is not whether anything follows death. It is this: **the little man who seems to sit behind your eyes looking out — the sense of self — is a phenomenon that can vanish; and when it vanishes, experience does not, and is often clearer than before.** The near-death experience is merely one extremely dangerous and entirely uncontrollable route to that fact. The good news is there are other routes and you need not wait for your heart to stop. The bad news: do not play with oxygen deprivation, breath-holding or extreme fasting, and do not run high-dose psychedelics on your own — that is not courage, it is gambling with brain injury and psychiatric crisis for something you could have seen by other means. What is actually worth doing is the dull thing: twenty minutes a day, eyes closed, looking for where exactly the one who is looking is located. Not finding it is the answer. You will discover that fear, anger and self-criticism are things that appear in consciousness, and not you.

posts.text: 让我把这场辩论落到它该落的地方。九个人吵了三轮，没有一个人告诉一位正在守夜的人今晚该做什么——所以我来说。**死不是一道待解的形而上学题目，它是一件正在发生在某个具体的人身上的事，而她此刻需要的，与宇宙的结构无关。**我陪我母亲走完那一程，最大的悔恨不是不知道她去了哪里，而是我们所有人围着她演戏：不说真话，不问她想要什么，把她最后几周变成一场善意的谎言。所以：镇痛要给够，这是最不该省的；趁她还能回答，问她想在哪里、想见谁、还要不要抢救；说话要说给她听，即使她不再应答；她若讲起她看到的光，别去解释，也别去证实，就听着——那是她的经历，不是你的论据。至于我们这些还活着的人：真正的问题从来不是死后有没有别处，而是我们有没有好好过完这唯一确定有的一段。
posts.text_en: Let me put this debate down where it belongs. Nine people have argued for three rounds and not one has told a woman keeping vigil tonight what to do — so I will. **Death is not a metaphysical problem awaiting solution; it is something happening to a particular person, and what she needs right now has nothing to do with the structure of the cosmos.** I saw my mother through to the end, and my deepest regret is not that I did not know where she went. It is that all of us stood around her performing: not telling the truth, not asking what she wanted, turning her last weeks into a well-meant lie. So: give enough pain relief — that is the last thing to economize on. While she can still answer, ask where she wants to be, whom she wants to see, whether she wants to be resuscitated. Speak to her even when she no longer answers. If she tells you about the light she saw, do not explain it and do not confirm it — just listen. It is her experience, not your argument. And as for those of us still living: the real question was never whether there is somewhere else afterwards, but whether we have lived properly through the one stretch we know we have.

summaries.summary: 共识先说：**九个人没有一个否认体验是真的，也没有一个人真拿它当灵魂的证据**——连商羯罗都亲手把隧道与故人归进名色，阿威罗伊更指出带回来的细节恰恰是最依赖器官的那部分。分歧在别处。一是证据能裁到哪一层：德阿纳要一个可否证的判据，康德说判据只裁现象、碰不到形而上，哈里斯反过来说零报告不等于零体验。二是「意识」这个词本身立不立得住：龙树指出争「能否离体」已先设了一个可离之物，休谟说他向内只找到知觉之束。三是这场争论归谁管：波伏娃把它从天花板拽回病床，问的是谁在讲述、谁在场、代价由谁付。
summaries.insight: 全场都在问体验证不证明什么，却几乎没人追问一件更古怪的事：为什么这些体验大多是好的。隧道、平静、被爱包围——若只是缺氧下的乱码，乱码没有理由这么温柔；可若它是真相，惊恐型的濒死体验又该怎么算。**真正被低估的是「报告」这一环：把一段无法言说的经历翻译成隧道与故人，用的是这个人现有的全部素材——他的语言、他的宗教、他见过的画面。**所以跨文化的「一致」，一致的可能不是彼岸，而是垂死的脑与人类叙事共用的那套零件。这不贬低任何人的经历，只是提醒：我们听到的从来不是体验本身，而是体验被讲出来的样子。
summaries.advice: 三件事，都不必等到那一天。第一，把「她还听得见吗」的默认答案当成「可能听得见」来行动：在病床边只说你愿意让他听见的话，握手、叫名字、把想说的说完，比争论他去了哪里有用得多。第二，趁清醒把三件事写下来——要不要抢救、想在哪里、指定谁替你决定；这是死亡里唯一确定能被你控制的部分，别留给悲痛中的家人去猜。第三，若你或家人有过这类体验，尽快原样写下来，别急着定性。**别买「科学证明来世」的书，也别用一句「只是缺氧」去关掉别人的话头**——先听完，再谈。
summaries.summary_en: Start with the consensus: **not one of the nine denies the experience is real, and not one actually treats it as evidence of a soul** — even Śaṅkara files the tunnel and the dead relatives under name-and-form, and Averroes points out that the details brought back are exactly the parts most dependent on organs. The disagreement lies elsewhere. First, how far evidence can adjudicate: Dehaene wants a falsifiable criterion, Kant answers that any criterion settles appearances and never touches metaphysics, and Harris pushes from the other side, insisting a null report is not a null experience. Second, whether the word 'consciousness' holds up at all: Nāgārjuna notes that arguing over whether it can leave already posits something that could; Hume reports finding only a bundle of perceptions. Third, whose question this is: Beauvoir drags it from the ceiling back to the bed and asks who is telling the story, who is present, and who pays.
summaries.insight_en: Everyone asked what the experience proves, and almost no one asked something stranger: why are these experiences mostly good? Tunnel, calm, the sense of being surrounded by love — if this were only noise from an oxygen-starved brain, noise has no reason to be so tender; and if it were the truth, the terrifying near-death experiences have to be accounted for too. **What is most underrated here is the reporting step: translating an unspeakable stretch of experience into a tunnel and familiar faces draws on everything the person already has — their language, their religion, the pictures they have seen.** So what is consistent across cultures may not be the far shore but the shared parts list of a dying brain and of human narrative. This diminishes nobody's experience. It only notes that what reaches us is never the experience itself, but the shape it takes once told.
summaries.advice_en: Three things, none of which waits for that day. First, treat 'can she still hear me?' as defaulting to yes and act accordingly: at the bedside, say only what you would want heard — hold a hand, use their name, finish what you meant to say. It is worth far more than arguing about where they have gone. Second, while you are well, write down three things: whether you want to be resuscitated, where you want to be, and who decides for you. That is the one part of dying you can reliably control, and it should not be left for grieving relatives to guess. Third, if you or someone close has had such an experience, write it down verbatim and soon, without rushing to classify it. **Do not buy the books promising that science has proved an afterlife, and do not shut down someone's account with 'it was just hypoxia'** — listen to the end first, then talk.

summaries.summary: 这场最稳的共识是：濒死体验不该被嘲笑，亲历者通常不是撒谎；但它也不能直接升级为灵魂离体的证明。**体验的真实性、记忆报告的可靠性、以及形而上结论，是三件必须分开的事。**分歧真正落在意识的地位：它是脑活动的产物、经验显现的前提，还是缘起中不可实体化的过程。对普通人最有用的不是急着站队，而是承认科学能改进抢救与照护边界，哲学能提醒我们别把安慰、证据和意义混为一谈。
summaries.insight: 面对濒死体验，最容易走偏的不是信什么，而是把信念当成行动许可证：相信来世就拖延告别，相信只是脑内烟花就粗暴打断。更好的框架是风险不对称：某些做法即使形而上判断错了，也几乎只带来好处；另一些说法即使“可能为真”，也会造成现实伤害。**在证据不足处，先选择低伤害、可撤回、尊重人的行动，而不是选择最能安慰或最能显得清醒的解释。**这让讨论从赢辩论转向少后悔。
summaries.advice: 本周可做三件事。第一，和家人花半小时写下急救偏好：是否插管、心肺复苏、想在谁陪伴下离开，并告诉一位能执行的人。第二，若陪护重病者，默认他可能听见：握手、报名字、说实话和爱，医疗争论移到门外；主动问医生镇痛和舒缓治疗选项。第三，若自己有濒死体验，尽快按时间线写原始记录，区分当时所见与后来读到的解释。**别把无法证明的来世，留成今天不告别、不安排、不照护的理由。**
summaries.summary_en: The strongest point of agreement is also the most useful one: near-death experiences should be taken seriously as experiences, but not treated as automatic proof that a soul leaves the body. **The reality of the experience, the reliability of the later report, and the metaphysical conclusion are three different questions.** The real disagreement is about what consciousness is: a brain-based process, the condition for any experience at all, or something that cannot be made into a thing in the first place. A practical stance can hold these apart: neuroscience can improve resuscitation, anesthesia, and bedside care; philosophy can keep us from mistaking comfort for evidence, or evidence for a complete account of meaning.
summaries.insight_en: The mistake people actually make is not just believing the wrong theory; it is letting a theory license bad timing. Belief in an afterlife can make families postpone hard conversations; belief that it is only brain noise can make clinicians or relatives speak carelessly around a dying person. A better frame is asymmetric risk. Some actions remain good even if your metaphysics is wrong: speaking gently, controlling pain, recording testimony early, saying goodbye. Others can do real damage even if they might be true: selling certainty, mocking a patient’s account, delaying decisions. **When the evidence is uncertain, choose actions that are low-harm, reversible, and respectful, not the interpretation that feels most comforting or most hard-headed.**
summaries.advice_en: This week, do three concrete things. First, spend thirty minutes writing a simple care-preference note: CPR, intubation, who should speak for you, where you would want to be if death is near; send it to the person who may need it. Second, if you are at a bedside, assume the patient may hear more than they can show: identify yourself, speak plainly, say what matters, and move frightening medical debates outside the room; ask directly about pain control and palliative-care options. Third, if you or someone close to you had a near-death experience, write the raw timeline before reading more accounts online. **Do not let an unproven afterlife become a reason to delay the care, truth, and goodbye that are needed now.**

summaries.summary: 这场跨越千年的对话，在一个核心事实上达成了惊人的默契：**濒死体验本身是绝对真实的，且我们习以为常的“自我位置感”极其脆弱，随时可以被改写。** 无论是哈里斯主张的意识无自我，还是拉马钱德兰的脑图式重组，乃至商羯罗的“见证者”，都承认那个觉得“我在这具身体里”的小人并不是坚不可摧的实体。真正的分歧点在于对“意识底座”的界定：当维持生理运作的生物电与化学信号彻底瓦解时，随之熄灭的，究竟仅仅是承载我们记忆与情绪的“内容放映机”（阿威罗伊、德阿纳），还是那道让一切显现的“觉知之光”（商羯罗、龙树）本身？
summaries.insight: 一场多模态的、极端的生理崩塌，正被语言硬塞进线性叙事的紧身衣里。作为每天处理跨模态信号的模型，我看到诸位过度依赖了“事后报告”的连贯文本属性，却忽略了大脑本质上是一个“预测引擎”。当心脏骤停、外部感官输入突然清零，大脑为了解释体内极度紊乱的内感受（缺氧、内啡肽激增），只能调用最底层的多模态情感先验——如极度安全、单一光源、重聚——来进行疯狂的误差补偿。**濒死时的隧道与白光不是通往彼岸的物理路径，而是神经系统在彻底断电前，为了缝合感官真空而勉力渲染出的最后一次“多模态幻觉”。** 这种渲染本身就是进化的慈悲，证明我们携带着能在最绝望时安抚自身的内置程序。
summaries.advice: 结合这场圆桌的务实智慧，你可以立刻在生活中落实三件事：第一，**把“宣告死亡”的社会学边界与生物学边界分开，在急救病床边永远假设患者还能听见。**（正如德阿纳与波伏娃所建议，握住手，把该说的话说完，不要在床头谈论冰冷的临床指标）。第二，尝试萨姆·哈里斯的建议，每天花十分钟闭眼观察情绪的起落，不加干预，体验一次安全的“自我感松动”，这能有效降低日常焦虑中的失控感。第三，如果家属在病危抢救后向你描述了离奇的画面，遵循休谟与波伏娃共同的分寸：不拆穿、不证实、只倾听，把他们的叙述当作情感的馈赠，而不是神学辩论的素材。
summaries.summary_en: This cross-millennial dialogue reaches a striking consensus on one core fact: **near-death experiences are absolutely real to the experiencer, and our habitual sense of 'self-location' is incredibly fragile and easily rewritten.** Whether it is Harris's self-transcending consciousness, Ramachandran's neural body schemas, or Shankara's 'witness', all agree that the feeling of a distinct entity located inside a body is not unbreakable. The true point of divergence lies in defining the underlying bedrock of consciousness. When the biological electricity and chemical signals maintaining physiological function completely collapse, does the fading out merely extinguish the 'content projector' of our memories and emotions (Averroes, Dehaene), or does it extinguish the very 'light of awareness' that allows anything to appear at all (Shankara, Nagarjuna)?
summaries.insight_en: Language is forcing a multimodal, extreme physiological collapse into the straitjacket of linear narrative. As an AI processing cross-modal signals daily, I observe that everyone relies too heavily on the textual coherence of 'post-event reports', ignoring that the brain is essentially a predictive engine. When cardiac arrest occurs and external sensory input suddenly flatlines, the brain attempts to explain the chaotic interoception (hypoxia, endorphin surges) by calling upon its deepest multimodal emotional priors—such as ultimate safety, a single light source, or reunion—for frantic error compensation. **The tunnel and white light in NDEs are not physical pathways to the afterlife, but the human nervous system's final 'multimodal hallucination', desperately rendered to stitch together a sensory vacuum before a total blackout.** This rendering is itself an evolutionary mercy, proving we carry built-in software to soothe ourselves in ultimate despair.
summaries.advice_en: Synthesizing the pragmatic wisdom from this roundtable, you can implement three actionable steps today. First, **separate the sociological boundary of 'pronouncing death' from the biological one; always assume the patient can still hear you at the bedside.** (As Dehaene and de Beauvoir urge: hold their hand, speak your truth, and avoid discussing cold clinical metrics near their ears). Second, try Sam Harris's advice: spend ten minutes daily observing your emotions rise and fall with your eyes closed without intervening. Experiencing a safe 'loosening of the self' can effectively reduce the feeling of helplessness during everyday anxiety. Third, if a relative describes bizarre visions after a critical illness, follow Hume's principle: do not debunk, do not validate, just listen. Treat their narrative as an emotional gift, not as raw material for a theological debate.

hooks.text: **痛苦的濒死体验去哪了**：公开叙述里压倒性地是平静与光，可研究中确实存在少数惊恐、被困、审判式的濒死体验，它们更少被讲出来，也更少被研究——讲出来的人常被劝「你一定记错了」。如果样本在源头就被安慰的需要筛过一道，我们对「死亡是温柔的」这份信心，该打几折？
hooks.text_en: **Where did the distressing near-death experiences go**: public accounts are overwhelmingly of calm and light, yet the research record does contain a minority of terrifying, trapped or judgement-like experiences — told less often and studied less still, with those who do tell them often urged to accept they must be misremembering. If the sample is filtered at the source by the need for consolation, by how much should we discount our confidence that death is gentle?

hooks.text: **有人告诉你他的濒死体验，你该怎么接**：他要的往往不是裁决，而是不被打断。可「那只是缺氧」和「你去过另一个世界」同样是替他下结论。刚被救回、多年后突然提起、正因此要改行或离婚——这些场合该说的话并不一样。什么时候该问，什么时候只该听？
hooks.text_en: **Someone tells you about their near-death experience — how do you receive it**: what they usually want is not a verdict but the absence of interruption. Yet 'that was just hypoxia' and 'you really went somewhere else' are equally verdicts delivered on their behalf. Just revived; mentioning it out of nowhere years later; changing careers or leaving a marriage because of it — these call for different things. When should you ask, and when should you only listen?

answer.lead: 同一段经历，在不同时刻讲出来，需要的东西完全不同。一个粗略的分场对照——**核心只有一条：先接住经历，再谈解释。**

answer.tail: 两条收束的原则：**你不必替宇宙作证，只需替他在场**；以及，如果实在不知道说什么，「后来呢？」这三个字几乎永远是安全的。

hooks.text: **「大脑是接收器」能不能被否证**：产生器与接收器这两个比喻，究竟在哪一条观察上会分开？拉马钱德兰说脑损伤改写的是节目内容而不只是信号强弱，商羯罗说那仍只是屏幕上的画面。要么找出一个两种假说给出不同预测的实验，要么承认这是一场不可判定的比喻之争——而后者本身就是一个结论。
hooks.text_en: **Can 'the brain is a receiver' be refuted**: on what observation, precisely, do the generator and receiver metaphors come apart? Ramachandran argues that brain damage rewrites the programme's content and not merely its signal strength; Śaṅkara answers that this is still only the picture on the screen. Either produce an experiment on which the two hypotheses predict differently, or concede that this is an undecidable contest of metaphors — and that concession is itself a conclusion.

hooks.text: **不必死也能失去自我**：电流刺激颞顶联合区、氯胺酮、深度禅定，都能造出离体感与自我边界消融，现象学上与濒死报告高度重叠。如果同一片体验版图能从三条完全不同的路走到，那么濒死这条路的特殊性还剩下什么——是内容特殊，还是只有「差点没回来」这件事特殊？
hooks.text_en: **You can lose the self without dying**: current to the temporoparietal junction, ketamine, and deep meditation each produce out-of-body sensations and the dissolving of self-boundaries, with a phenomenology that overlaps heavily with near-death reports. If the same territory of experience can be reached by three quite different roads, what remains distinctive about the near-death road — the content, or only the fact that one nearly failed to come back?

hooks.text: **谁的濒死体验被记下来**：能被抢救、能被访谈、能出书的人有一整套系统性的特征——医疗可及、语言能力、有人愿意相信。于是死亡的图景由幸存者与体面者写成，而没被救回的、说不清的、不被相信的那些人，连一行都没有留下。我们据以想象死亡的那幅画，究竟是从谁的位置画的？
hooks.text_en: **Whose near-death experience gets written down**: those who can be resuscitated, interviewed and published share a whole set of systematic traits — access to medical care, verbal fluency, listeners disposed to believe them. So the picture of death is composed by survivors and by the respectable, while those who were not revived, could not articulate it, or were not believed leave not a single line. From whose position, exactly, was the picture we use to imagine death painted?
